title: introduce-hsm-rotation-operator-and-terraform-provider-for-pkcs11-keys
author: Amina Patel
release_notes: Adds a new HSM rotation operator (optional) and Terraform PKCS#11 provider module. Backwards compatible; opt-in via Helm value enableHsmOperator=true. See upgrade notes for migration steps.
description:
Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private with strict key custody requirements asked for an operator to manage HSM-backed key lifecycles (rotate asymmetric keys, publish certificate updates, reconcile PKCS#11 slots) without manual operator intervention. This PR delivers an opt-in controller (HSMRotationOperator), a Terraform provider wrapper to provision HSM objects and helper scripts, and Helm chart toggles + migration path for customers currently using KMS or Vault-wrapped keys.

What this change contains: consolidated changes across the installer, Helm chart and Terraform modules so users can provision keys (or point to existing PKCS#11 objects) and enable automatic rotation and certificate re-issuance. Key pieces: 1) controller/hsm-operator: a lightweight reconcile loop that watches HSMKey custom resources, triggers rotation within configured TTL, performs CRC checks on the public key material, and triggers a rolling secret update for components consuming the key. Operator supports PKCS#11 backends (SoftHSM for tests) and an HSM plugin interface for cloud HSMs and on-prem devices (YubiHSM2, Luna, Thales). 2) terraform/modules/hsm-pkcs11: module to create PKCS#11 objects via vendor-provider and to emit a redwood_hsm_key resource that the private installer can consume. 3) helm/redwood-private: new values.enableHsmOperator, values.hsm.providerConfig (base64 PKCS11 config or reference to sealed secret), and a new chart hook to create necessary CRDs. 4) migration helper scripts under tools/hsm-migration that translate existing KMS/Vault keys into HSMKey CRs with validation and dry-run mode.

Upgrade/migration path: default behavior is no-op; operator is disabled by default. To opt in: update Helm values to enable the operator, install the Terraform module (or point to existing PKCS#11 config), and run tools/hsm-migration migrate --dry-run to validate resources. For clusters using Vault-wrapped keys, the migration script supports a key-wrap-to-pkcs11 flow where it exports wrapped key material into an intermediate sealed secret, then asks operator to unwrap into HSM via vendor provider. We include a recommended canary rollout: enable operator in a single control-plane node pool, run key sync for one service, and watch telemetry for signing errors for 48h.

Security considerations: operator runs with least privilege RBAC only to HSMKey CRs and secrets in the installer namespace. Terraform provider credentials should be stored as sealed-secrets; Helm supports specifying sealedSecrets.enabled=true to keep provider credentials encrypted. HSM access uses PKCS#11 and requires explicit mounting of device sockets (documented). All networked HSM traffic is recommended to be routed inside a private VPC.

Testing & verification: adds unit tests for operator reconciliation, integration tests using SoftHSM in GitHub CI, and an e2e which deploys a tiny TLS-terminating demo service that rotates its certs every 24h (simulated). CI was flaky on first run due to SoftHSM image pull; fixed in commit that pins test image to retry policy.

Operational notes: operator writes rotation events to the new metric redwood_hsm_rotate_total and emits a span with tags hsm.vendor and hsm.key_id for tracing. We also add an alert template in observability/alerts to catch failed rotations >3 tries. Rollback: operator has a safe-backoff and a 'revert-to-old-key' flag on the HSMKey CR which will copy previous key version back to the consuming secret. See notes_on_rollback for more details.

Files of interest and examples are listed below; small config snippet to show Helm values usage: 
values.yaml snippet: 
  enableHsmOperator: true
  hsm:
    provider: pkcs11
    providerConfig: "base64:LS0tUEtDUyMxMS1jb25maWcn..."

Related: ENG-1342 for operator design, SEC-241 for threat model review.

e2e_test_results: passed: demo service rotated cert twice in staging cluster without downtime
notes_on_rollback: Operator supports revert-to-old-key boolean on HSMKey CR. For full rollback, set revert-to-old-key=true and operator will copy previous key version to the consuming secret and trigger rolling restart of dependent deployments. Terraform changes are additive; to rollback provider-managed PKCS#11 objects use terraform state rollback. If Helm upgrade fails, run helm rollback release --namespace redwood-private <revision>. Manual steps for emergency rollback are documented in docs/private/hsm-operator.md.
changelog_entry: Added HSMRotationOperator (opt-in), Terraform pkcs11 module, Helm flags to enable HSM support, and migration tooling. Backwards compatible and disabled by default.
